newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-May/Jun gas oil trades at 98cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-May/Jun gas oil trades at 98cts.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted in lacklustre trading late afternoon on Tuesday with the May/June spread narrowing slightly due to the weaker front month, brokers said.
"The market is drifting down slightly but there are no clear signals yet," one broker said.
May swaps were last quoted at $25.50/$25.55, down 10 cents from Monday, brokers said. May traded earlier in the day at $25.53, they said.
The May/June backwardation traded earlier at 97 and 98 cents, down from $1.00/$1.10 per barrel on Monday.
Traders said the narrowing of the time spread was mainly due to the softer front month rather than stronger buying interest for June.
"The whole market is softer but things could change later today if Hin Leong comes in and buys another two million barrels," one trader said.
Hin Leong, together with two other traders, have bought nearly 18 million barrels of diesel since March 3.
Last week the companies took the market by storm when they chalked up a one-day purchase record of 2.44 million barrels.
But despite the large purchase, physical prices have instead trekked a steady downward path from a high of about $28.75 per barrel to around $26.00 over the past two months.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with May quoted at $98.25/$99.00, brokers said.
